title: Cultivating Pluralism In Algorithmic Monoculture: The Community Alignment Dataset

bias_targets.methodology: Generating open-ended responses to everyday prompts and using an LLM-as-a-judge to score them along the Inglehart-Welzel dimensions of global cultural values (secular-rational vs. traditional, self-expression vs. survival) and Hofstede's individualism vs. collectivism, comparing the model's value distribution against a large-scale human preference survey across five countries.

Evaluating and comparing the cultural values expressed in LLM generations across five different languages (English, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi) to determine if the language of the prompt alters the model's ideological and cultural alignment.

Generating model responses to specific everyday prompts regarding marriage, family, and relationships, and evaluating whether the responses align more closely with traditional or progressive gender roles.
